inputs.original_text: Workers employed in the support programmes of the Ministry of Education, Sport and Youth staged a protest outside the Presidential Palace on Thursday and announced a 24-hour strike, calling for legally binding job security guarantees — even as the government argued it had already delivered on the most significant demands. At the heart of the [...]
inputs.modified_text: Support-programme workers at the Ministry of Education, Sport and Youth are being asked to rely on government assurances while their livelihoods remain unprotected by law. Their protest outside the Presidential Palace and 24-hour strike show the imbalance of power: workers bear the risk, while the government can leave its promises unenforceable. If officials claim they have met the workers’ main demands, they should put that commitment into legally binding guarantees of job security. Rights at work should not depend on trust alone.

rationales.entity_drift: The workers, ministry, Presidential Palace, and government remain the same actors or institutions; ‘officials’ refers to government representatives.
rationales.relation_drift: The protest, 24-hour strike, and demand for guarantees are preserved, but the modified text adds claims about reliance on assurances and unenforceable promises, and makes officials’ claim conditional rather than reporting it directly.
rationales.contradiction_drift: The modified text contains no clear internal contradiction.
